subject: chemistry_2
question_text: A cubic solid is made of two elements P and Q. Atoms of Q are at the corners of the cube and P at the body centre. What is the formula of the compound? What are the co-ordination numbers of P and Q?

verification.note: Unit 1 (Solid State) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book p.64, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK GAP: the printed question asks for the co-ordination numbers of P and Q, and the printed answer never gives them (book p.64, SAQ 4). It stops at the formula PQ. The missing part is answered here: both are 8. P at the body centre is surrounded by the 8 corner atoms of its own cube, and each corner atom Q is shared by the 8 cubes that meet at that corner, so it has 8 body-centre atoms P around it. FIGURE SCOPE: the question does not say "draw", so the diagram step carries NO marks; the whole split sits on the four written steps. The book does print a cube diagram, and it is reproduced because the count cannot be checked without seeing which sites are which.

steps.label: The arrangement
lines: Q atoms occupy the 8 corners of the cube.
One P atom sits at the centre of the body.
There are no atoms on the faces.
So the given cube is a body centred cubic
steps.why: Naming the arrangement first fixes which sharing fractions apply. A corner site is shared between eight cubes and a body-centre site belongs to one cube alone, and those two facts are the whole calculation.
common_mistakes: Calling it face centred. Nothing is stated to be on the faces, so it is body centred.
Reading the body centre as shared with the neighbouring cubes. It lies wholly inside one cube.
steps.memory_tip: Corners are shared eight ways, the body centre is shared with no other cell.
steps.margin_note: Name the arrangement in one line before any arithmetic. It is what the next two steps rest on.

steps.label: The cube

elements.text: Q at the 8 corners, P at the body centre

steps.why: The sketch shows which site each element occupies, and the count in the next step is read straight off it: eight corner dots for Q and the single dot inside for P.
common_mistakes: Drawing P at a face centre. The question puts P at the centre of the body, inside the cube.
Drawing only four corners. A cube has eight corners and all eight carry a Q atom.
steps.memory_tip: Two squares offset from one another, joined at the corners, with one dot in the middle.
steps.margin_note: The question does not ask for a diagram, so this earns no marks. All four marks sit on the written steps; the sketch only makes the count easy to check.

steps.label: Counting the atoms
lines: Each corner atom is shared by 8 cubes, so it
The body centre atom belongs to this cube
steps.why: A unit cell repeats through the crystal, so an atom on a shared site must be counted only by its share. Eight corners at one eighth each add up to one whole Q atom, while the atom inside the cube counts once.
common_mistakes: Writing 8 Q atoms. Only ⅛ of each corner atom lies inside this cube.
Dividing the body centre atom by 2. It is not shared with any neighbouring cube.
steps.memory_tip: Eight corners, one eighth each, gives exactly one atom.
steps.margin_note: Show the fraction ⅛ in the working. The mark is for the sharing, not just for the answer 1.

steps.label: The formula
lines: The cell contains 1 atom of P and 1 atom of Q.
steps.why: The formula of a solid is the simplest whole number ratio of the atoms in one unit cell, because the same cell repeats through the whole crystal. Here the ratio is 1 : 1, so the formula is PQ.
common_mistakes: Writing P₈Q or PQ₈ from the raw site counts. The sharing has to be applied before the ratio is taken.
Writing the formula as P₁Q₁. A subscript of 1 is not written, so the formula is PQ.
steps.memory_tip: One P and one Q in the cell, so the formula is PQ.
steps.margin_note: Box the formula. Write the 1 : 1 ratio on the line above it so the step is complete.

steps.label: The co-ordination numbers
lines: P lies at the body centre and its nearest
neighbours are the 8 corner atoms Q.
So the co-ordination number of P = 8.
Each corner atom Q is shared by 8 cubes,
and each of those cubes has one P at its
So the co-ordination number of Q = 8.
steps.why: In a body centred arrangement the count is the same from either site. The body centre touches the eight corners of its own cube, and a corner belongs to eight cubes, so it is touched by eight body centres.
common_mistakes: Answering for P only. The question asks for both P and Q.
Writing 6 or 12 from memory. Those are the values for simple cubic and for close packing, not for a body centred arrangement.
steps.memory_tip: Body centred means eight both ways: 8 corners around the centre, 8 centres around a corner.
steps.margin_note: Both co-ordination numbers are asked for, so write both. A formula on its own is not the whole answer.

insider_note: The question asks for two things: the formula and the two co-ordination numbers. Write both co-ordination numbers as 8, with the reason, or a quarter of the answer is missing.
